findings.title: Tray "Settings" runs ShowSettings again even when a settings dialog is already open.
findings.body: The window now stays alive while hidden, so a dialog left open is still open the next time the window is shown. The issue this PR closes (#467) describes exactly that: open Settings, hide to tray, then come back. If the user picks tray "Settings" at that point, `ShowSettingsCommand.Execute(null)` starts a second run. `AsyncRelayCommand.Execute` ignores `CanExecute`, which is why the in-window button is greyed out. A second settings dialog then either waits on the dialog lock and reopens as soon as the user closes the first, or DialogHost throws because it is already open. Fix: only show the window when a dialog is already open, e.g. `if (_mainViewModel.ShowSettingsCommand.CanExecute(null)) _mainViewModel.ShowSettingsCommand.Execute(null);`.

held.title: The start-hidden check runs on every Loaded and depends on dialogs already being open.
held.body: `StartOptions.Current.IsInitiallyHidden` never changes after startup, so this handler hides the window every time `Loaded` fires. If Avalonia raises `Loaded` again when a hidden window is shown, then with `--start-hidden` every tray click or hotkey would show the window and hide it at once. I could not confirm how Avalonia behaves after `Hide`/`Show`. The `!DialogHost.IsOpen` check also only sees dialogs that are already open when this handler runs. A startup dialog opened after an await, or from a Loaded handler that runs later, would be left on a hidden window. Fix: make the hide one-shot (unsubscribe or use a flag after the first run) and hide before the startup dialogs are scheduled.
